# Scoring Methodology

How to read every cell in the matrix, and why the scale has five values.

## Why five

A four-point scale forces an unknown into a zero. That is not a neutral
formatting choice — it is an assertion that a vendor lacks a capability when all
you actually know is that nobody has written it down.

This has already happened once in this programme. Phase 0 recorded *"exactly zero
competitors have an IPR module"* across 11 competitors. Phase 9 falsified it: Wellspring
for Tech Transfer, Helikon Labs, Commercify and SINT·OTRI all implement patent,
licence and spin-out workflow. None had been assessed as *absent*; they had
simply not been found.

So the scale is:

| Score | Meaning | Burden of proof |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | Differentiator | Vendor markets it as a distinguishing capability |
| 2 | Native | Full implementation, standard part of the product |
| 1 | Partial | Basic or incomplete implementation |
| 0 | **Absent** | **Positive evidence of absence.** Requires `absence_note`. |
| U | **Unknown** | Neither evidenced nor ruled out |

## The rule the build enforces

Every vendor scoring **0** on any dimension carries an `absence_note` naming what
the published scope was checked against. `data_p10_matrix.py::validation()` fails
the build if a note is missing or under 40 characters.

This is the mechanism that keeps the matrix from becoming confident fiction.

## Absence basis — because not all absences are equal

| Basis | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **COMPLETE** | The vendor publishes a full feature table. A dimension missing from it is strong evidence of absence. |
| **PARTIAL** | The vendor publishes marketing prose only. A dimension it does not mention may simply be undocumented. |

The `absence_basis` column publishes which applies per vendor. A zero on a
PARTIAL list is a weaker claim than a zero on a COMPLETE one, and the matrix
refuses to flatten the distinction.

![Evidence honesty](../_exports/charts/phase10/p10_03_evidence_honesty.png)

## Evidence coverage

Every row publishes the share of its 15 cells that are not `U`.

A low number means the row is sparse — and **sparseness is the finding, not a
defect to be papered over**. Incubatee (SCIP) scores 0% coverage: Phase 9
verified the vendor exists but its scope is not published in enough detail to
score anything. Recording fifteen zeros for it would have been a fabrication.

## Market position is derived, not asserted

| Tier | Rule |
|---|---|
| VERIFIED | reviews ≥ 20 **and** a NAMED_REFERENCE customer |
| PROVEN | reviews ≥ 10, **or** a NAMED_LOGO customer |
| PARTIAL | breadth ≥ 6 **and** at least one named customer |
| UNPROVEN | none of the above |

An earlier rubric awarded ESTABLISHED on breadth alone. That was **circular** —
breadth is derived from this matrix's own scores, so it would have rated a
well-scoring vendor as established regardless of whether anyone had ever used it.
ESTABLISHED now requires external evidence.

These are **evidence tiers, not quality tiers**. A vendor can be UNPROVEN and
still be excellent.

## Evidence grades for named customers

| Grade | Meaning |
|---|---|
| NAMED_REFERENCE | a named person, role and organisation |
| NAMED_LOGO | an organisation named by the vendor, unreferenced |
| VENDOR_CLAIM | asserted by the vendor, unverified |
| UNKNOWN | no evidence either way |

**A VENDOR_CLAIM is not evidence of a deployment.**

## What was not done

- No competitor was contacted. **0 conversations.**
- No product was trialled.
- No pricing was negotiated.
- Absence was assessed against **published material only**, never against the
  product itself.
